disclaimer: Original forced-choice vignette — not the Political Compass Organisation quiz. Social items revised so both poles sound equally civic.

economic.label: Economic
economic.description: Redistribution and public provision vs markets and private ownership.

social.label: Social
social.description: Personal liberty and free expression vs shared order, cohesion, and institutional norms.

a.text: Government should heavily tax high incomes to fund public services.

b.text: People should keep most of what they earn; taxes should stay low.

a.text: Healthcare works best when private markets and insurance compete.

b.text: Healthcare is a right that should be broadly guaranteed by the public.

a.text: Large corporations need strong regulation to protect workers and consumers.

b.text: Heavy regulation mostly slows growth and should be kept light.

a.text: Private ownership is generally more efficient than state ownership.

b.text: Major industries like energy or rail can fairly belong in public hands.

a.text: A strong welfare safety net is essential even if it costs more in taxes.

b.text: Welfare should be narrow so people are pushed toward work and self-reliance.

a.text: Free trade usually benefits consumers and should be the default.

b.text: Trade policy should protect domestic jobs even if prices rise.

a.text: Wealth inequality at current levels is a serious problem to fix.

b.text: Unequal outcomes are acceptable if people have a fair chance to compete.

a.text: Employers and employees should negotiate freely with limited special union privilege.

b.text: Unions should have strong power to bargain for workers.

a.text: Housing and rents need public tools so shelter stays affordable.

b.text: Building more privately and easing rules is the better path to affordability.

a.text: Market innovation and carbon pricing beat central climate planning.

b.text: Climate goals justify large public investment and industrial planning.

a.text: Personal lifestyle choices should be left to adults, even when neighbors disapprove.

b.text: Communities work better when shared moral expectations guide public life.

a.text: Public debate needs shared standards about harmful speech to stay constructive.

b.text: Open debate matters more than shielding people from offensive speech.

a.text: Adult drug use should be treated mainly as a health and autonomy issue.

b.text: Communities need firm drug rules to protect kids and public safety.

a.text: More monitoring of public spaces is worthwhile if it prevents serious crime.

b.text: Privacy from government monitoring matters even when it makes policing harder.

a.text: Schools should emphasize independent thinking more than national loyalty.

b.text: Schools should teach pride in shared civic traditions alongside academics.

a.text: Changing unfair laws should go through official channels, not street disruption.

b.text: Peaceful protest and civil disobedience can be needed when institutions stall.

a.text: Immigration policy should lean open, with opportunity for people seeking a better life.

b.text: Immigration policy should lean careful, with clear limits that protect social cohesion.

a.text: Public institutions should reflect inherited cultural and spiritual traditions.

b.text: Public policy should stay neutral on religion and treat belief as private.

a.text: Adults should be free to form families and identities without pressure to match tradition.

b.text: Stable, conventional family patterns deserve public encouragement because they help kids.

a.text: Police and security agencies need enough latitude to keep order effectively.

b.text: Police and security agencies need tight limits so rights are not eroded.
